newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL'S CAPELLO PREPARES FOR BITTERSWEET TITLE FIESTA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL'S CAPELLO PREPARES FOR BITTERSWEET TITLE FIESTA.

text.p: Real Madrid coach Fabio Capello goes into Saturday's game with neighbours Atletico aware that he may end the match as both hero and villain.
A draw will be enough to give Real their 27th Spanish championship.
But Capello knows the title celebrations would mark the end of the uneasy truce that has existed since he decided to leave the club at the end of the season.
Although Capello has not yet talked of his plans for the future, all signs point to his returning to AC Milan.
Head-hunted from the Italian side with the aim of turning round Real after one of their worst seasons on record, Capello has comfortably lived up to the expectations placed in him.
The high point of his season was January's 4-1 drubbing of reigning champions Atletico.
But despite the result of the away game, Capello refuses to underestimate the task on Saturday.
"Atletico are a great team, and it was bad luck that they didn't get to the final of the European Cup."

Capello -- three times a European Cup finalist as manager -- could once again find himself in the bizarre position of missing out on playing the premier continental competition despite having won two of Europe's top leagues in successive seasons.
But while Milan players carried Capello shoulder-high in the San Siro stadium last year, he will be lucky to be treated the same way by the Real squad on Saturday.
His no-nonsense style has led him to clash with some of the top Real stars, particularly strikers Davor Suker and Predrag Mijatovic.
Even when his side were 5-0 up against Extremadura, Capello let loose a ferocious tirade on his players from the sidelines.
"If they don't do what you tell them in training, you get angry," he said.
Characteristically Capello is reluctant to succumb to the triumphalism that has swept through Real supporters since second-placed Barcelona slipped up at struggling Hercules two weeks ago.
"People who talk about parties and celebrations are mad," said Capello.
"I don't like saying I have something until I can touch it,"
Capello's caution contrasts with that of many Real fans.
Madrid police are already taking precautions to prevent some of the wilder and more dangerous excesses that have crowned Real title celebrations in recent years.
The expectation surrounding Saturday's game is such that queues have been forming all week for the most expensive tickets ever for a game in the Santiago Bernabeu stadium.
The cheapest tickets start at 3,000 pesetas ($20), with the best costing five times more.
